notes: Adding a LoRA is no longer transcription work. Paste a Civitai model page link into any LoRA row's URL field — Settings or a character's — and the row fills itself from Civitai's API: the real download link, the model's name, its trigger words, and WHEN worked out from the model's own metadata (18+ models gate on 18+, models tagged as styles ride every photo, and anything else gets its Civitai tags as keywords so it only loads on matching shots). A raw download link fills only the blanks, so rows you already tuned stay yours. Next to Test LoRAs there is now Civitai favorites, and the character editor has Browse Civitai favorites: heart a LoRA on civitai.com and it appears in a sheet here with its preview picture, ready to add in one tap with everything pre-filled — models without a FLUX file are shown but greyed out, since FLUX is the only base either image engine runs. And the biggest thorn: getting files onto the RunPod volume no longer requires renting a pod by hand and typing wget into a terminal. Install LoRAs to volume, under Your own GPU, asks the endpoint what the volume already holds, lists what's missing, and then either rents a tiny CPU pod for a few minutes that downloads everything onto the volume and deletes itself (a few cents), or copies the identical script for pasting into any pod terminal if the management API isn't reachable from the browser. Downloads resume if interrupted and half-finished files never sit under a loadable name.
